constants.description: Voltage rating of standard US 15 A and 20 A receptacles
constants.source_publisher: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR)
constants.quote: All 125-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles installed in bathrooms or on rooftops shall have ground-fault circuit-interrupter protection for personnel.
constants.note: The rating is above the 120 V nominal supply, which makes the limit lenient.

constants.description: Highest receptacle rating on a standard US 15 A or 20 A branch circuit
constants.source_publisher: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR)
constants.locator: Paragraph (b)(4)(ii), Table S-5 'Receptacle Ratings for Various Size Circuits'
constants.note: Table S-4 of the same section limits the cord-and-plug load on a 20 A receptacle to 16 A, so the full 20 A rating is lenient.

assumptions: The receptacle rating is not stated; the 20 A rating is used, which is the most lenient.
notes: Losses inside the product only lower the output further, which makes this bound lenient.

verdict_reason: The claims that could be tested are physically plausible (Power budget (output ≤ input)). This does not confirm that the claims are true.
